newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London up, boosted by Hang Seng record.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London up, boosted by Hang Seng record.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London gained across the board on Wednesday as the buying spree, which earlier pushed shares in Hong Kong to record highs, spilled over into London, dealers said.

The Hang Seng London Reference index climbed 117.82 points to finish at 16,101.00, after the Hang Seng jumped 211.12 points to a record close of 15,983.18. Earlier in the Hong Kong session, the Hang Seng set an all-time high of 16,055.19.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc led the advance, following the sharp gains by shares in British banks in London. HSBC gained HK$3.12-1/2 to HK$266.12-1/2.

Property and utility stocks were keenly sought, after a good run earlier in Hong Kong. Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties rose 35 cents to HK$95.85, while Cheung Kong climbed 57-1/2 cents to HK$81.32-1/2.

Dealers attributed the advances by shares in Hong Kong and London to the recent record closes on Wall Street and to investors becoming more positive on property shares, the sector having been out of favour since the return to Chinese rule on July 1.
